ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized representatives against FINTRAC's sanctions lists, Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, the UN Security Council consolidated list, and the OFAC SDN list where any US nexus exists; screening shall be repeated at incorporation filing and periodically thereafter as a condition of AML compliance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) – Business Name and Corporate Search / NUANS Name Search Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French, or in another script with a mandatory transliteration into Roman letters; names that are deceptively similar to an existing Alberta name, an existing trade name, or a prescribed name will be rejected; Alberta Corporate Registry accepts names containing numerals, punctuation, and initials subject to NUANS confusion criteria.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant may file a 'Request for Reconsideration of Name Search' with the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the NUANS result, accompanied by written representations, the original NUANS search report, and a $50 reconsideration fee (non-refundable); if the reconsideration is denied, a new name search must be commissioned and fresh Articles of Incorporation submitted within 90 days of the new search date.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Allowed for a low-risk PropTech SaaS entity provided the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address in Alberta, accepts service of process during normal business hours, and the registered office is not a P.O. Box; a registered office address must be disclosed in the Articles of Incorporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% to 10% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by Alberta Corporate Registry or FINTRAC within the first three years, absent a regulatory trigger (e.g., PEP involvement, sanctions hit, or high-risk payment activity); for a domestic standard-risk SaaS with ACH/Stripe payment rails, baseline likelihood is approximately 5%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 6-20 (incorporation), s 15 (designation as unlimited liability corporation), s 101 (registered office), s 103 (corporate records); Supplementary provisions under the Alberta Business Corporations Act Regulation, AR 202/2011
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Corporate Access online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 2) together with Notice of Registered Office (Form 3) and Notice of Directors (Form 1) filed through Corporate Access
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC); shares may be issued for nominal or unpaid consideration and no escrow account is required. Liability exposure is governed by the unlimited liability characteristic: shareholders remain jointly and severally liable for the corporation's debts, liabilities, and obligations to the extent provided under the ABCA and the Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED: 1. The Certificate of Incorporation is acknowledged and all subscribed common shares are hereby allotted to the incorporators in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation. 2. The registered office of the Corporation is established at [Registered Address], Alberta, and statutory records shall be maintained at that address. 3. The directors named in the Articles are confirmed in office. 4. [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Corporate Secretary, each authorized to open banking accounts and engage legal counsel and accountants. 5. The financial year-end is fixed and the corporate seal and share certificate books are adopted. 6. Officers are authorized to execute all required registrations with the Canada Revenue Agency and Alberta authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, via authorized NUANS service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS Name Search Request containing up to three proposed corporate names. Each name must include the mandatory legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'. Pay the prescribed search fee (CAD 10 for electronic search) and obtain the NUANS report, which is valid for 90 calendar days from issuance.
required_dossiers: List of up to three proposed corporate names with ULC designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused as confusingly similar or otherwise non-distinctive, obtain a revised NUANS report with alternative names and re-file the reservation; the registry will process the corrected submission within the same service window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Incorporation and Initial Statutory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporate Access online filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 2 Articles of Incorporation, designating the company structure as an unlimited liability corporation, defining the authorized share structure, naming first directors, and stating any restrictions on business. Prepare accompanying Form 1 (Notice of Directors) and Form 3 (Notice of Registered Office). Attach the NUANS report and obtain each director's consent to act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried for deficient schedules or missing signatures, the registry will issue a deficiency notice; cure by amending the specific schedules and re-submitting through Corporate Access, addressing every written deficiency before payment of re-filing fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Documents and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Forms electronically via Corporate Access and pay the prescribed filing fee (CAD 200 online, CAD 250 paper). Upon review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which is conclusive evidence of the entity's existence under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
required_dossiers: Form 1 and Form 3 completed and executed
Electronic payment receipt for filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, correct the identified errors and re-submit with the applicable re-filing fee; no administrative appeal is required for non-substantive corrections, and resubmission is processed under the standard priority queue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Adoption of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the newly incorporated Alberta ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting of the board of directors, adopt the First Board Resolution covering share allotment, registered office confirmation, officer appointments, banking authorities, adoption of By-law No. 1, and fixing the financial year-end. Open the corporate minute book, issue share certificates, and maintain statutory registers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address is queried by the registry, provide documentary evidence of lease, ownership, or written authorization granting physical access for records; file a Notice of Change of Registered Office if relocation is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online portal) and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply through the CRA Business Registration Online service for the federal Business Number, GST/HST account (mandatory when annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000), corporate income tax account, and payroll deductions account. Alberta administers its provincial corporate tax through the CRA under a tax collection agreement; no separate provincial corporate registration form is required. Obtain a municipal business licence where the office is physically located.
required_dossiers: Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number)
Articles of Incorporation and Initial Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA rejects or suspends the Business Number application, correct the entity details and resubmit Form RC1 online; CRA processing is generally completed within 48 to 72 hours once all mandatory data fields are valid.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade and Municipal Business Licensing Authority (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Licensing Department)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Municipal Business Licence for Information Technology and Cloud-Based Services (no sectoral manufacturing or operating permit is applicable to pure-play SaaS undertakings under Alberta law)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (Regulatory Assurance Division)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is a cloud-based PropTech SaaS platform with no physical plant, construction, discharge, or resource extraction; no environmental registration or approval is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the core software operations. Office premises must comply with municipal solid waste and recycling by-laws, lease covenants, and, if auxiliary backup generators or cooling units are installed, applicable municipal noise limits and the Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives for combustion emissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupancy permit and fire safety certification issued under the Alberta Safety Codes Act, including fire extinguisher placement and emergency exit compliance; structural load clearance for the leased office premises; workplace occupational health and safety clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2 and the OHS Code for computer-based office operations, including ergonomic and electrical safety standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — federal GST/HST and corporate income tax administration; CRA My Business Account portal at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html. Alberta corporate income tax is collected by the CRA under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act collection agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must obtain an Alberta corporate access number or extra-provincial registration through the Alberta Corporate Registries (CORES). It then applies to the CRA via Form RC1 or online My Business Account, providing incorporation documents, Canadian registered office or agent address, director particulars, and principal business activity. The CRA issues a 9-digit Business Number (BN) with an RT (GST/HST) account and, where applicable, an RP payroll account. Non-residents must designate a Canadian representative for service of notice and satisfy CRA non-resident registration validation protocols.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An Alberta ULC is by default a taxable Canadian corporation under the Income Tax Act (Canada) but is pass-through eligible: (i) subsection 96(2.1) Income Tax Act election may treat a foreign-owned ULC as fiscally transparent where the shareholder jurisdiction also treats it as transparent; (ii) US check-the-box election on Form 8832 may classify the ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership; (iii) GST/HST closely related corporation election under section 156 of the Excise Tax Act (Form GST25) taxes intra-group supplies at nil consideration; (iv) GST/HST group registration election under section 239 (Form GST10) consolidates filing; hybrid mismatch positions must be documented to prevent double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST with no provincial sales tax component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (small supplier threshold measured by worldwide gross revenues from taxable supplies over the preceding four calendar quarters; mandatory registration applies upon exceedance, elective below threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate. GST/HST registrants must file returns electronically using GST/HST NETFILE or EDI where required by the CRA, and must retain books and records, including electronic records, in a prescribed machine-readable format. Alberta has no provincial e-invoicing regime; voluntary adoption of PEPPOL or other business software partner e-invoicing standards is permitted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of SaaS or computer software to a non-resident who is not a GST/HST registrant is zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act (sections 7 and 23), provided the supply is not made to a resident of Canada, is not in respect of real property situated in Canada, and is not in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada. For PropTech real estate SaaS, the underlying property management or rental screening services must relate to real property located outside Canada for zero-rating to apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA export declaration, where physical goods are involved)
Bill of Lading or House Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign bank wire confirmation evidencing payment from the non-resident
Commercial invoice and signed SaaS subscription or software licensing agreement
Non-resident status and nil-registration declaration obtained from the recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA can reassess and claw back ITCs and zero-rating refunds within the normal four-year reassessment period, with no limitation period where misrepresentation or fraud is established. Penalties under the Excise Tax Act include a false statement or omission penalty (section 285(1)) of the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax understated, a gross negligence penalty (section 285(2)) of the greater of CAD 250 and 50% of the net tax understated, and compound interest under section 280. The exporter bears the burden of proving the non-resident status of the recipient, the foreign situs of the service, and receipt of funds within the documented period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential banking oversight and FINTRAC for AML compliance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a fully liberalized currency regime for both current and capital accounts. The Canadian dollar is freely convertible and there is no general foreign exchange control approval requirement for cross-border remittances, profit repatriation, dividend payments, or capital investment. The only residual statutory powers are emergency reserve powers under the Currency Act and repealed Foreign Exchange Control Regulations; none are currently active. Profit remittances from an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) to non-resident shareholders are subject to normal Income Tax Act Part XIII withholding and tax treaty considerations, but no FX conversion approval or central bank license is needed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export proceeds surrender obligations and no mandatory conversion ratio for foreign currency receipts. Exporters and service providers such as PropTech/SaaS businesses may retain export revenues in foreign currency accounts or convert them at their discretion. For Canadian tax reporting under the Income Tax Act, the ULC must account for foreign exchange gains and losses pursuant to section 261 and maintain an appropriate functional currency election if substantial CAD reporting is not practical.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. Offshore digital EMI or fintech-only banking providers are not a legally independent substitute for a tier-1 Canadian bank account. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), any cross-border payment service operating into Canada must hold a Canadian Money Services Business (MSB) registration with FINTRAC or operate solely through a bank-registered agent. Offshore EMIs may be used as supplementary settlement rails (e.g., digital wallets for SaaS receipts), but all capital escrow, FX conversion, and trade settlement for the Alberta ULC must route through a Canadian scheduled bank or authorized provincial credit union. Direct integration with Stripe Billing and ACH Direct is viable as a payment acceptance adjunct to the primary bank clearing account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FINTRAC/PCMLTFA KYC rules require verifiable identification of all directors, officers, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners above 25%. For a newly incorporated Alberta ULC, a physical branch visit by at least one director or senior officer (or a bank-recognized notarized agent) is generally mandated at first account opening. Several tier-1 Canadian banks offer hybrid remote onboarding with certified/notarized documentary packages and a video interview for non-resident principals, provided the entity is in good standing with the Alberta Corporate Registry and all UBOs are fully identified. Remote-only opening is not consistently available and should not be relied on; a physical presence or notarized in-person verification is the preferred and compliant path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited liability structure combined with non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide Alberta Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, Articles of Incorporation, full beneficial ownership register, specimen resolution authorizing account opening, passport copies for all directors and UBOs, and explanatory disclosure of the ULC's pass-through eligibility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client/tenant deposit flows for a PropTech rental screening platform
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the institutional platform license exemption assessment, operational flow-of-funds diagram, master service agreement template, privacy and data protection policy demonstrating no borrowing, lending, or deposit-taking activity, and a lawyer's opinion confirming the entity does not constitute a bank or money services business under Canadian law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection and intercompany disbursements from a related parent
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide intercompany loan or share subscription agreement, board resolution supporting the capital contribution, audited or reviewed financial statements evidencing the funding's commercial purpose, tax residency certificates of parent entities, and a source-of-wealth statement covering the ultimate funding source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk foreign correspondent bank jurisdiction appearing in the payment chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain an optimized routing map using only Canadian and OECD-listed correspondent banks, include a sanctions self-certification, provide copies of the ULC's own OFAC/CSIS screening policy, and produce the bank's electronic KYC prior notice record for any wire involving heightened-risk jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfers into the Alberta ULC capital escrow account must use SWIFT MT103 with explicit narrative referencing the capital subscription or shareholder loan. Recommended ISO 20022/World Bank BOP purpose code: 'G11' (Direct Investment) or equivalent 'Debt settlement / intercompany loan' category for loan injections. The Canadian correspondent bank should attach a Certificate of Funds Origin and the ULC must file any required CRA Reporting of Unlisted Disposition or AML Suspicious Transaction Report if the amount exceeds CAD 10,000. Retain the corporate resolution, capital call schedule, and ULC shareholder register as trailing documentation to prove the commercial and non-money laundering purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for software licensing fees, rent screening vendor payments, and international subcontractors should be executed via SWIFT MT103 through the tier-1 Canadian bank with automated dual-signatory control. For high-value or recurring disbursements (threshold > CAD 250,000), a Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP600 (SWIFT MT700) may be issued, supported by standby LC in favour of the ULC. Low-value SaaS subscription and recurring customer refunds are cleared via ACH Direct and Stripe Billing rails, with immediate settlement into the ULC operational account; all cross-border outbound wires must indicate the appropriate transaction purpose code to the destination bank and comply with the destination country's turnover currency rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD outright deliverable forwards (plain vanilla spot/forward contracts) with Canadian chartered banks
CAD/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDF) as cash-settlement overlay where physical delivery is not commercially desirable
CAD/EUR and CAD/GBP rolling forward hedges for subscription revenue diversification
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for intercompany shareholder loans
FX swaps on spot/forward pairs for temporary liquidity rebalancing between CAD operational and USD capital escrow accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, filed through an authorized registry agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file annual returns for two consecutive years may result in involuntary dissolution after notice. Registry-agent service charges may be additional; no separate statutory late-filing penalty is specified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 corporation income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's tax year-end; any balance generally is due within two months, or three months for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and interest may apply to unpaid tax; repeated or extended non-filing may lead to collection action and prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general revenue or asset threshold applies. Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, a non-distributing corporation may dispense with an auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution for the relevant financial year; otherwise, an auditor must generally be appointed. Confirm eligibility and any shareholder-resolution requirements for the specific ULC.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises and ASPE generally available to private enterprises. A ULC is generally treated as a corporation for Canadian income tax; pass-through treatment should not be assumed.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not currently impose a general statutory significant-control register or annual UBO confirmation filing for Alberta corporations. Keep the securities register and corporate records current when ownership changes; separately assess federal, tax, and foreign-jurisdiction disclosure obligations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or securities register
Records must be maintained at the registered office or another permitted records office; electronic records are permitted if statutory requirements are met.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300-800 annually; Alberta requires a registered office in the province but does not require a registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-10,000 for a small private company; actual fees depend on transaction volume, complexity, and audit scope.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined (Federal 15% Part I general rate + Alberta 8%; Alberta Innovation? no)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No preferential rate for general-purpose ULC; R&D SR&ED? Canadian-controlled? Foreign-controlled ULC not eligible for small business deduction; 5% Alberta?
